description: Routing of specialist roles and required convergence gates by project class. Roles are registered in config/agent-roles.json.

product.label: Product scope, journeys and acceptance criteria

information-architecture.label: Sitemap, navigation, taxonomy and content hierarchy

ux.label: Task flows, state coverage and recovery

content.label: Copy quality, voice and claim discipline

brand.label: Brand fidelity against supplied and observed evidence

architecture.label: Data model, auth, tenancy and API boundaries

design-system.label: Token, component, motion and accessibility contract completeness

visual.label: Rendered visual quality, authorship and business specificity. minimumScore is the professional-output bar a candidate must reach before it may be promoted; minimumCriterionScore stops a strong average hiding one badly failing criterion; reworkIterationBudget bounds how many times a failed candidate may be revised before the set is decided without it.
visual.$scaleNote: minimumScore is DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED at 8.5 while the scale beneath it was redefined. Raising the number against an uncalibrated scale would have been the cheap fix and would have measured nothing: the reviewer had no definition of any point on 0-10 and was told the bar in its own prompt, so 8.5 meant "whatever a model returns when asked for 8.5". Under the v2 rubric 8.5 is a mean over thirteen anchored criteria — including resistance to generic AI design language and memorability, neither of which was previously asked — issued by a reviewer that is not told the target and must justify every score of 8 or above. It is a materially harder bar at the same number.
visual.$topScoreNote: A score of 10 is not reachable through this gate alone. It additionally requires a recorded pairwise benchmark comparison finding no material gap, a holistic tier of benchmark-class, and no scoped criterion below 8. See TOP_SCORE_CONTRACT in tooling/lib/visual-rubric.mjs.
visual.$deterministicBoundary: design-lint decides facts: contrast, reduced-motion handling, mechanically detectable repetition and competing primary actions. It was deliberately NOT extended to the AI-slop motifs (gradient headlines, rounded cards, pill overuse, centred alignment, uniform padding). Every one of those is legitimate in some context and generic in others, and a rule that banned them would encode a second template in place of the first. They are put to the critic as the ai-slop-resistance criterion, which asks whether the pattern has a reason to exist here rather than whether it exists.
visual.$evidenceNote: Evidence coverage now counts routes as well as viewports, and the evidence a review rests on caps what it may claim: one route at one width supports a professional reading and no more. A home page cannot prove a website.

functionality.label: Acceptance journeys work in a real browser

responsive.label: Composition holds at every declared width

accessibility.label: No serious/critical automated failures and manual findings resolved

seo.label: Crawlability, metadata, structured data and evidence-backed local signals

security.label: Auth, tenancy, input, secrets, storage and deployment boundaries

provenance.label: Every published fact and asset retains source and rights state

tests.label: Coverage, regression protection and deterministic checks

launchability.label: The build is genuinely ready to launch

state-completeness.label: Every reachable, user-visible state is designed and evidenced

journey-closure.label: Each acceptance journey is complete end to end, not merely implemented

marketing-site.label: Marketing / local-business website
marketing-site.notes: Brand, art direction, conversion copy and SEO/AEO carry real weight here.

content-site.label: Content / editorial site
content-site.notes: Same shape as a marketing site; collections and editorial rhythm dominate composition.

b2b-saas.label: B2B SaaS application
b2b-saas.notes: Architecture, tenancy and security dominate. No separate brand/art-direction stage by default.

consumer-app.label: Consumer application
consumer-app.notes: Adds brand and art direction to the application pipeline.

ai-app.label: AI-first application
ai-app.notes: Application pipeline plus brand/art direction; AI capability budgets are part of the architecture stage.

internal-tool.label: Internal tool
internal-tool.notes: Deliberately omits research, brand, art direction, marketing content, SEO and red team to avoid spending context on work the project does not need.
